feed.title: Boeing white-collar union contract vote results expected today
feed.summary: Voting on Boeing's contract offer to its largest white-collar union, SPEEA, concludes today, with results anticipated by mid-afternoon in Seattle. While Boeing offered terms described as better than expected to avoid a strike, neither the engineers nor the technicians unit councils fully endorsed the offer, with technicians recommending rejection. A key point of contention in the proposed four-year contract is the 3% cap on inflation-based wage increases, which some members believe will lead to salaries falling behind inflation.

feed.title: Engine issue causes Delta flight to North Carolina to return to Atlanta airport

feed.title: Walmart promises price cuts after $2.9B tariff refund
feed.summary: Walmart announced it will use a $2.9 billion tariff refund to implement price cuts for consumers, aiming to stimulate spending amidst slower sales growth. feed.title: TMUS Builds on Strong Service Revenue Growth: Can it Continue?

Despite strong competition from AT&T and Verizon, T-Mobile's focus on network and customer experience is bolstering retention, though its stock price has declined while competitors show growth in broadband subscribers.

feed.title: MSI Expands Drone Portfolio With D-Fend Deal: Will it Drive Growth?
feed.summary: Motorola Solutions (MSI) is acquiring D-Fend Solutions for $1.5 billion, expanding its public-safety portfolio with advanced counter-drone technology. D-Fend's unique method of neutralizing rogue drones by taking control, rather than jamming, and its extensive customer base across 30+ countries, are expected to create cross-selling opportunities and accelerate MSI's growth. The acquisition positions MSI to compete with companies like Axon Enterprise and RTX Corporation in the growing airspace security market, though long-term financial gains depend on successful integration and scaling of the technology.

feed.title: HPQ Set to Report Q3 Earnings: What's in Store for the Stock?

The company's performance is likely to be driven by strong momentum in its Personal Systems business, particularly from AI PCs and premium PCs, alongside growth in gaming products. However, rising memory prices and increased inflationary pressures on oil and transportation costs are expected to negatively impact profitability, especially in the Print segment.

feed.title: Aptiv stock slips as 2026 guidance and valuation reset
